correctness.rationale: The total-population equation gives the exact full-system eigenvalue -mu. Eliminating that direction yields a five-dimensional tangent Jacobian whose entries are derived algebraically from the published endemic equilibrium. Exact Fraction arithmetic gives an affine shifted determinant with a unique zero at R_cross. In odd real dimension, positive nonzero determinant rules out all shifted eigenvalues lying in the closed left half-plane, proving a tangent eigenvalue has real part greater than -mu below the crossover. The standalone verifier reconstructs the determinant from the baseline parameters. The claim does not infer stability on the whole interval from sampled numerics.

value.rationale: The exact crossover answers a natural question created by the source's own spectral conclusion: how close to the transcritical threshold can the demographic mode remain dominant? The answer is an exact, uniquely defined collision on the published one-parameter branch, and it identifies a near-threshold regime omitted by the 0.01 grid where another linear mode is necessarily slower. This is directly relevant to interpreting convergence times close to eradication and is not an arbitrary parameter slice.
